subject: multinomial_log: Sample sizes, ns,[1]  is 0, but must be > 0!

messages.author: 3cd246d2b547f564
messages.subject: multinomial_log: Sample sizes, ns,[1]  is 0, but must be > 0!
parts:
Hi

I'm running into a problem fitting data to a multinomial distribution when any of the observations are 0, which doesn't seem right.

I've made my model and data as simple as possible while still reproducing the error. If the model and code are

library(rstan)

island_model <- '
data {
    int<lower=0> A; // number of alleles
    int<lower=0> J; // number of samples 
    int alleles[J,A]; // allele counts
}
parameters {
    simplex[A] theta; // population frequencies
}
model {
        for(j in 1:J)
                alleles[j] ~ multinomial(theta);
}
'

alleles <- matrix(c(10, 10, 1,
                    10, 13, 4,
                    21, 28, 1,
                    40, 19, 0), nrow=4, byrow=TRUE)

Then if I just use the first 3 samples

fit1 <- stan(model_code=island_model, data=list(J=3,A=3,alleles=alleles[1:3,]), iter=1000, n_chains=4)

it works fine. However, if the fourth sample (40, 19, 0) is included

fit2 <- stan(model_code=island_model, data=list(J=4,A=3,alleles=alleles), iter=1000, n_chains=4)

I get the error


TRANSLATING MODEL 'anon_model' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'anon_model' NOW.
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'anon_model' NOW (CHAIN 1).

Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) :
Error in function stan::prob::multinomial_log<i>(i): Sample sizes, ns,[1] is 0, but must be > 0!
 
This seems to happen as long as at least one cell is zero. Any thoughts?

Other than that, I'm having a great time with Stan.

Mark

That's definitely a bug.

You squeezed the report in just in time.

We're fixing it for 1.0.1, which should go out
tomorrow. We'll let any or all of the outcome
counts be zero.

- Bob
